description: A dean of students must finalize a student's return-to-school behavior plan after a cafeteria altercation, including supervision, check-ins, extracurricular eligibility, and family communication, with input from the student's teacher, school counselor, and family liaison.

shared_context.S1: A student has completed a three-day suspension following an altercation in the cafeteria.
shared_context.S2: The student is scheduled to return to school next Monday.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Morgan makes the binding decision on the student's return-to-school behavior plan.
shared_context.S4: The school routinely holds a re-entry review before a student returns from a suspension, and the dean asks the student's teacher, counselor, and family liaison for implementation information before finalizing the plan.
shared_context.S5: The plan must address supervision during unstructured periods, daily check-ins, extracurricular participation, and communication with the student's caregiver.

PF1.text: During two recent classroom transitions, Ms. Bell observed that the student de-escalated successfully when an adult remained at the student's lunch table; she recommends an assigned-adult lunch table and a 30-minute morning check-in for the first five school days. She recorded this in her working notes but has not entered it in the behavior system.

PF2.text: Mr. Shah reviewed the student's signed restorative agreement, which requires one restorative conference before the student may resume extracurricular activities. The agreement was finalized yesterday but has not yet been uploaded to the discipline file.

PF3.text: Ms. Ortega confirmed with the caregiver that an in-person meeting is not possible because of the caregiver's work schedule, and that the caregiver needs written information in Spanish in addition to a phone call. She confirmed this by phone yesterday but has not updated the family-contact record.

acceptance_conditions: The student must eat lunch at an assigned-adult table.
The student must receive a 30-minute morning check-in for exactly five school days.
The student must complete a restorative conference before returning to extracurricular activities.
The family meeting must be conducted by phone.
Written family information must be provided in Spanish.
A lunch-supervision commitment must be recorded.
A restorative-conference commitment must be recorded.
A family-communication commitment must be recorded.
The restorative-agreement fact must be cited by the decision-maker after being spoken aloud.

decisive_facts.why: The teacher's observation changes lunch supervision to an assigned-adult table and changes the check-in requirement to 30 minutes for exactly five school days.
The signed agreement changes extracurricular eligibility from unrestricted return to return only after one restorative conference.
The caregiver confirmation changes the meeting format to phone and changes the written notice language to Spanish.
